滸山鎮 is Hushan Town (山 = shan); "Hushen" misrenders the place name.

In winter Chancellor Kule'na impeached Degeli for privately altering the court diary (Qijuzhu) and accused him and Xu Yuanmeng of mutual puffery. Both men were stripped of office and imprisoned.
起居注 is the court diary of the emperor's activities (Records of Rising and Repose), not the Veritable Records (實錄).

內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary (大學士).
The emperor spared Xu's life. He wore the cangue for three months, received a hundred lashes, and was sent to the Sinister Works.
The emperor spared Xu's life. He wore the cangue for three months, received a hundred lashes, and was consigned to the Xinzheku, the bondservant labor service of the Imperial Household.
辛者庫 transcribes Manchu sin jeku, the Imperial Household bondservant labor service; "Sinister Works" is a misleading calque.
In 1702 he served as examiner for the metropolitan provincial examination.
In 1702 he served as examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination.
順天鄉試 is the Shuntian provincial examination; "metropolitan" invites confusion with the metropolitan examination (會試) in s0142.
The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers. Only You Ruo's promotion was approved, ranking below Zisi; the rest was shelved.
The matter was referred to the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers. Only You Ruo's promotion was approved, ranking below Zixia; the rest was shelved.
子夏 is Zixia (Bu Shang), not Zisi (子思, Kong Ji).
Jiang Tingxi, whose style was Yangsun, came from Changshu in Jiangnan and was the younger brother of Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Chen Xi.
Jiang Tingxi, whose style was Yangsun, came from Changshu in Jiangnan and was the younger brother of Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Jiang Chenxi.
陳錫 here is the given name of Jiang Tingxi's elder brother 蔣陳錫 (Jiang Chenxi); "Chen Xi" wrongly treats 陳 as a surname.
In 1726 errors in his translation of memorials cost him his office. He was ordered to serve among the grand secretaries while continuing to handle translation.
In 1726 errors in his translation of memorials cost him his office. He was ordered to serve among the sub-chancellors of the Grand Secretariat while continuing to handle translation.
內閣學士之列 means the ranks of the sub-chancellors of the Grand Secretariat, not grand secretaries (大學士).
When the Qianlong Emperor came to the throne, Xu was assigned to the Southern Study and soon appointed grand secretary.
When the Qianlong Emperor came to the throne, Xu was assigned to the Southern Study and soon appointed sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary (大學士).
He rose through repeated promotions to grand secretary.
He rose through repeated promotions to sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary (大學士).
He also memorialized requesting repair of the Wansongling Academy; the emperor granted the plaque "Spreading Culture on the Zhe Waters," and he therefore requested that the academy be named Fufen.
He also memorialized requesting repair of the Wansongling Academy; the emperor granted the plaque "Spreading Culture on the Zhe Waters," and he therefore requested that the academy be named Fuwen.
敷文 is read Fuwen; "Fufen" misromanizes the academy name.

The emperor ordered Grand Secretary He Guozong and others to bring instruments and maps and conduct an on-site survey with Director-General Qisuole and Governor Chen Shirui. They recommended adopting Jiang's proposals.

The emperor ordered Sub-chancellor He Guozong and others to bring instruments and maps and conduct an on-site survey with Director-General Qisule and Governor Chen Shiguan. They recommended adopting Jiang's proposals.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor, not a grand secretary; 齊蘇勒 reads Qisule (蘇 su, 勒 le); 陳世倌 reads Chen Shiguan (倌 guan), not Shirui.
After four promotions he became a grand secretary.
After four promotions he became a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary (大學士).
He was posthumously honored as Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Treasury funds were granted for his funeral, state funeral honors were bestowed, and he received the posthumous title Wenk.
He was posthumously honored as Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. Treasury funds were granted for his funeral, state funeral honors were bestowed, and he received the posthumous title Wenke.
諡文恪 is Wenke; "Wenk" is a truncated romanization.
He was ordered to administer the Three Treasuries jointly with Prince Guo, Yunli, and granted the hereditary rank of first-class adaha gushan.
He was ordered to administer the Three Treasuries jointly with Prince Guo, Yunli, and granted the hereditary rank of first-class adaha hafan.
阿達哈哈番 transcribes adaha hafan; "gushan" (固山) is a different Manchu term.
Censor Hu Ding proposed encouraging reclamation of wasteland along Hunan's lakes and ordered Pu to investigate and report.
Censor Hu Ding proposed encouraging reclamation of wasteland along Hunan's lakes, and Pu was ordered to investigate and report.
令溥察議 is an imperial order to Pu; the English wrongly makes the censor Hu Ding the one who ordered Pu.
His son Zhen passed the palace examination.
His son Cheng passed the palace examination.
檙 (木+鼎, a variant of 朾; Kangxi Dictionary reading 宅耕切) is read cheng; "Zhen" has no basis.
Cici was first appointed prefect of Chuxiong in Yunnan and later rose to vice minister of revenue.
Ciqi was first appointed prefect of Chuxiong in Yunnan and later rose to vice minister of revenue.
賜棨 is read Ciqi (棨 qi); "Cici" misreads the second character.
Or else granary grain is sold off and the proceeds embezzled; when turnover comes, it is reckoned at two cash per shi, and successors cannot afford to buy grain to make up the shortfall.

Or else granary grain is sold off and the proceeds embezzled; when turnover comes, it is reckoned at two qian (two-tenths of a tael) per shi, and successors cannot afford to buy grain to make up the shortfall.
錢 here is the silver weight qian (mace, 1/10 tael), not copper cash.
He also wrote: "In Jiangxi's disaster-stricken prefectures and counties, relief kitchens were established for porridge distribution, and rice prices reached one tael and three or four cash per shi.
He also wrote: "In Jiangxi's disaster-stricken prefectures and counties, relief kitchens were established for porridge distribution, and rice prices reached one tael and three or four qian per shi.
錢 here is the silver weight qian (1/10 tael), not copper cash.

For the new Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi garrisons he set cash equivalents for grain rations—one tael per shi at Yongshun, eight cash at Baojing and Sangzhi—reflecting the higher rice prices on the Miao frontier.

For the new Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi garrisons he set cash equivalents for grain rations—one tael per shi at Yongshun, eight qian (0.8 tael) at Baojing and Sangzhi—reflecting the higher rice prices on the Miao frontier.
八錢 is eight qian of silver (0.8 tael), not eight copper cash.
Huang, courtesy name Jinwei, was a Han bondsman of the Plain White Banner.
Huang, courtesy name Jinwei, was a member of the Han-martial (Hanjun) Bordered White Banner.
漢軍 are the Chinese-martial banners, not bondservants; 鑲白 is the Bordered White Banner, not the Plain White (正白).
He began as a clerical secretary, passed the examination for Hanlin drafter, and rose to reader.
He began as a clerical secretary, passed the examination for drafter of the Grand Secretariat, and rose to reader.
內閣中書 is a drafter of the Grand Secretariat, not a Hanlin post.
The people thereafter lived free of floods and named the structure Prefect Bai's Dike.
The people thereafter lived free of floods and named the structure Lord Bai's Dike.
白公 is an honorific "Lord Bai"; Bai Huang was governor, not a prefect.
When Yongzheng took the throne in the sixty-first year, Huang was appointed acting grand secretary.
When Yongzheng took the throne in the sixty-first year, Huang was appointed assistant grand secretary.
協辦大學士 is assistant grand secretary, a regular post, not an acting appointment.
His grandfather Yuan tutored him from hand-copied editions of the Spring and Autumn Annals and Mongol-script versions of the Records and Han.
His grandfather Yuan hand-copied the Spring and Autumn Annals with its Inner and Outer Traditions, the Records, and the Han, and taught them to him as primers.
蒙文 here means texts for elementary instruction (童蒙); there is no Mongol script in this Shandong Han family's tutoring.

Grand Secretary Fang Bao memorialized: "The ever-normal granary grain was originally fixed at keeping seven parts and selling three each year; the southern provinces have low, damp ground and should be allowed to adapt measures to local conditions."

Sub-chancellor Fang Bao memorialized: "The ever-normal granary grain was originally fixed at keeping seven parts and selling three each year; the southern provinces have low, damp ground and should be allowed to adapt measures to local conditions."
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary.

In the sixth year Censor Zhong Yongtan accused Grand Secretary Xu Wangyou of summoning the Nine Ministers to mourn at a commoner's house in the capital; Guolin had attended as well. An inquiry by princes and senior ministers found the charge baseless.

In the sixth year Censor Zhong Yongtan accused Sub-chancellor Xu Wangyou of summoning the Nine Ministers to mourn at the house of the commoner Yu Changgeng in the capital; Guolin had attended as well. An inquiry by princes and senior ministers found the charge baseless.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor, not a grand secretary; the idiomatic text also drops the named commoner 俞長庚 (Yu Changgeng).
A corrupt custom added surcharges twice, reaching eight or nine cash, called "equalization."
A corrupt custom added surcharges twice, reaching eight or nine qian (tenths of a tael), called "equalization."
錢 here is the silver weight qian (1/10 tael), not copper cash.
In the third month of the sixth year he asked to retire; the emperor praised him warmly, granted the request, and invested him as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
In the third month of the sixth year he asked to retire; the emperor praised him warmly, granted the request, and invested him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent upon retirement.
太子太師 is the Grand (senior) Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; the junior rank is 太子少師.

Learning that Congdian's son Mao was still a boy, the emperor sent a grand secretary and a reader-in-waiting to manage the funeral, a minister without portfolio and six guards to pour libations, and ordered local officials to escort the coffin home.

Learning that Congdian's son Mao was still a boy, the emperor sent a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat and an academician reader to manage the funeral, a minister without portfolio and six guards to pour libations, and ordered local officials to escort the coffin home.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor, not a grand secretary; 侍讀學士 is an academician reader.
The court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wende.
The court granted state funeral honors and posthumously titled him Wenduan.
諡文端 is Wenduan; "Wende" would be 文德.
Years later he was made drill captain in the Firearms Brigade and inherited his grandfather Shangyi's second-class ada hafan title.
Years later he was made drill captain in the Firearms Brigade and inherited his grandfather Shangyi's second-class adaha hafan title.
阿達哈哈番 transcribes Manchu adaha hafan; "ada hafan" drops a syllable.
Campaigning under Grand General Prince Fu against Galdan, he smashed the camel formation at Ulan Butung and was promoted to commandant.
Campaigning under Grand General Fuquan, Prince Yu, against Galdan, he smashed the camel formation at Ulan Butung and was promoted to commandant.
裕親王福全 is Fuquan, Prince Yu (裕); "Prince Fu" conflates his personal name with the princely title.
That autumn he reported that crows had devoured the locusts and the autumn crop was thriving.
In the autumn of the second year of Yongzheng he reported that crows had devoured the locusts and the autumn crop was thriving.
The idiomatic text drops the explicit date 雍正二年秋, leaving "that autumn" without a referent year.
That winter he presented an uncarved jade seal with twin dragon knobs that Huangpu fishermen had hauled in; the emperor bestowed a four-clawed dragon rank badge.
That winter he presented an uncarved jade seal with twin dragon knobs that Huangpu fishermen had hauled in; the emperor bestowed a surcoat with four dragon roundels.
四團龍補服 is a surcoat bearing four dragon roundels; it says nothing about claws.
Sun Zhu, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
Xunzhu, of the Dong'e clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.
遜柱 reads Xunzhu (遜 xun); "Sun Zhu" misreads the first character, and the Manchu name is not a surname-plus-given-name form.
Sun Zhu began as a clerk and was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.
Xunzhu began as a clerk and was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.
遜柱 reads Xunzhu (遜 xun); "Sun Zhu" misreads the first character, and the Manchu name is not a surname-plus-given-name form.
Sun Zhu ran the Ministry of War for sixteen years, repeatedly memorializing on its affairs and conducting extensive reviews and reforms.
Xunzhu ran the Ministry of War for sixteen years, repeatedly memorializing on its affairs and conducting extensive reviews and reforms.
遜柱 reads Xunzhu (遜 xun); "Sun Zhu" misreads the first character, and the Manchu name is not a surname-plus-given-name form.
In the eleventh year he retired; he died at age eighty-four. An edict praised Sun Zhu as "honest, generous, and conciliatory," and imperial funeral rites were granted.
In the eleventh year he retired; he died at age eighty-four. An edict praised Xunzhu as "honest, generous, and conciliatory," and imperial funeral rites were granted.
遜柱 reads Xunzhu (遜 xun); "Sun Zhu" misreads the first character, and the Manchu name is not a surname-plus-given-name form.
He served in turn as Hanlin reader-in-waiting, grand secretary, and vice minister of the Mukden Ministry of Works.
He served in turn as Hanlin academician reader, sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, and vice minister of the Mukden Ministry of Works.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary; 侍讀學士 is an academician reader.
In 1723 he was summoned to court and appointed grand secretary.
In 1723 he was summoned to court and appointed sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat.
內閣學士 is a sub-chancellor of the Grand Secretariat, not a grand secretary.

When General Gar proposed establishing a coastal navy, Yin Tai argued that Lüshun and Tianjin already had naval forces and that Jinzhou, Fuxing, and Gaizhou could be covered by rotating patrols; new units would cost a fortune and do little for coastal surveillance.

When General Gar proposed establishing a coastal navy, Yin Tai argued that Lüshun and Tianjin already had naval forces and that Jinzhou, Fuzhou, and Gaizhou could be covered by rotating patrols; new units would cost a fortune and do little for coastal surveillance.
錦、复、蓋諸州 are Jinzhou, Fuzhou (复州) and Gaizhou; "Fuxing" is not the place named.
In 1703 he was promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.
In 1703 he was promoted to supervisor of the household of the heir apparent.
詹事 is the supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent (詹事府), not a tutor.
When the Yongzheng emperor came to the throne, he was ordered to serve as guardian of the Yongzheng mausoleum.
When the Yongzheng emperor came to the throne, he was ordered to serve as guardian of the Jing Mausoleum, the Kangxi Emperor's tomb.
景陵 is the Jingling, tomb of the Kangxi Emperor, not a Yongzheng mausoleum (the Yongzheng Emperor was still living).
In 1733 he asked to retire on account of age, was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was allowed to leave office; his son Bangzhi, a Hanlin compiler, was sent home to care for him.
In 1733 he asked to retire on account of age, was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was allowed to leave office; his son Bangzhi, a Hanlin compiler, was sent home to care for him.
太子太傅 is the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the junior rank is 太子少傅.

When the Shizong Emperor punished Yin Zhi and Yin Tang, Xu Yuanmeng said: "The two men's crimes merited execution; I pray that Your Majesty, mindful of brotherly affection, may temper their punishment and spare their lives."

When the Shizong Emperor punished Yunsi and Yuntang, Xu Yuanmeng said: "The two men's crimes merited execution; I pray that Your Majesty, mindful of brotherly affection, may temper their punishment and spare their lives."
允禩 and 允禟 are the imperial princes Yunsi and Yuntang (允 yun, 禩 si, 禟 tang); "Yin Zhi"/"Yin Tang" misread the characters and treat 允 as a surname.
